transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-11
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (CTO, Aurora), Ethan Marshall (Eng Lead, Aurora), Samir Patel (DevOps, Aurora)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Customer is exploring Redwood for inference layer—wants to understand SDK support for LangChain/LlamaIndex, options for running behind their gateway/proxy, controls for rate limits and quotas, and observability hooks to integrate with existing telemetry. Security and deployment model (VPC vs dedicated) are top evaluation criteria.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:06] Priya: Hi I'm Priya, CTO at Aurora, we run a multi-tenant infra for customers, interested in adding chat/assistant features but need tight control over latency and data.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan here, lead on the app platform, we own the gateway and the server side integrations.
[00:20] Samir: Samir, DevOps, I'll own orchestration and security checks.
[00:24] Lena: Great, Marcus and I from Redwood — Marcus is our solutions engineer.
[00:28] Marcus: Hey all, quick agenda, SDKs and integration patterns, traffic characteristics, security/deployment requirements, and next steps.

[02:05] Marcus: To start — we support first-class SDKs in our REST and official SDK (Node/Python/Go), and we have reference patterns for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Have you used either?
[02:13] Ethan: We have some Langchain experiments, but mostly through internal wrappers. We saw LlamaIndex mentioned in some examples but haven't used it in prod.
[02:24] Priya: Key for us is how to wire Redwood behind our gateway. We want the gateway to do auth and quota enforcement, not leak keys to client devices.
[02:36] Marcus: Totally. Two common patterns — sidecar approach where each service calls the Redwood SDK directly with a local sidecar/proxy, or a central gateway/proxy that forwards requests and applies auth/rate-limits. We recommend central gateway for multi-tenant control, but sidecar reduces cross-service latency for high-throughput paths.
[02:55] Samir: For sidecar we'd need an internal network token exchange; for gateway we need per-route quotas. How granular are your quotas?
[03:07] Lena: We expose per-api-key and per-route rate limiting, plus request and token quotas at enterprise level. You can scope quotas to project or customer.
[03:15] Ethan: Is rate-limiting enforced at the edge or by Redwood runtime?
[03:19] Marcus: Our control plane issues tokens and enforces soft quotas at the gateway; enforcement happens in the ingress layer of Redwood's runtime. For Dedicated/Private you can push policy enforcement into your VPC or use our sidecar.

[05:00] Priya: Security — SOC 2, SSO, KMS integrations, audit logs — we need these for vendor approval. How mature are those?
[05:12] Marcus: We have SOC 2, SAML SSO integrations, RBAC, and audit logs. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management. I'll share our security whitepaper.

[06:30] Ethan: On observability — we run Prometheus, Grafana, and distributed tracing (Jaeger). Can we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency metrics into our telemetry?
[06:42] Marcus: Yes — Redwood exposes metrics via Prometheus endpoints and has tracing hooks (OpenTelemetry). For token-level cost breakdowns we emit metrics and logs that can be ingested by your cost pipeline; we also have hooks to push events to Kafka or your existing logging.

[08:00] Samir: About integrating with LangChain/LlamaIndex — does Redwood have example connectors? We don't want to re-implement prompt templates.
[08:12] Marcus: We maintain a repo with LangChain wrappers and examples for LlamaIndex ingestion. The sample flow uses our SDK with a provider class; for LlamaIndex we show how to persist indexes and run retrieval-augmented generation using Redwood endpoints. I'll share the link.
[08:30] Priya: Any gotchas with streaming responses and reconnects? We need streaming to the UI with sub-second begins.
[08:39] Marcus: Streaming supported via server-sent events/websockets in our SDKs. If the connection drops we support resume from last token via KV cache in the runtime — though resume semantics depend on model and sequence length. Sometimes the transcript might be slightly duplicated on reconnect.

[10:12] Ethan: About models — do you host open models or do we bring our own?
[10:18] Lena: We have a model catalog of curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. You can run hosted models on Redwood's infrastructure, reserve Dedicated capacity, or bring your own model to Private deployment (on-prem or in VPC).
[10:30] Ethan: Latency targets? Our SLAs expect p95 < 300ms on short chat prompts.
[10:36] Marcus: For small context O(64 tokens) p95 <300ms typically on Dedicated; hosted varies by model. Private with co-located GPUs can meet stricter latency. We can run benchmarks in pilot to validate.

[12:00] Priya: For the gateway pattern — do you recommend a pass-through or token-exchange approach? We want to avoid storing keys in the gateway.
[12:12] Marcus: Token-exchange is safer: gateway authenticates users, then mints short-lived internal tokens for Redwood calls. We have a token broker pattern in our docs. If you'd rather keep a central API key, you can restrict via per-route policies.

[13:45] Ethan: Rate-limits again — can we set dynamic quotas per tenant? E.g., tiered plans.
[13:52] Lena: Yes, per-tenant quotas and rate-limits are supported. We also have soft-fallbacks and automatic throttling policies. You can integrate with our API to change quotas programmatically.

[15:30] Samir: Observability hooks — will Redwood's metrics include model-level breakdowns (which model served each call) and cost per-call?
[15:36] Marcus: Yes, we tag metrics with model, route, and tokens consumed. Cost per-call is emitted as a metric you can multiply by pricing tiers; we also send aggregated billing reports.

[17:00] Priya: We run heavy RAG (retrieval augmented generation) for internal search — the embedding pipeline is heavy. What about embedding throughput and batching?
[17:12] Marcus: Embedding endpoints support batching and asynchronous ingestion. For high throughput you can use our dedicated pools with configurable batch sizes and burst capacity. Batching reduces unit cost but increases latency; there is a knob.

[19:10] Ethan: Do you have a recommended architecture for LlamaIndex + Redwood + our existing vector DB?
[19:18] Marcus: Typical pattern — ingest into LlamaIndex connectors that write vectors to your vector DB, use Redwood for embedding generation and for LLM calls. We provide sample code wiring LangChain/LlamaIndex to our SDK. If you want to keep model and vectors in-house, use Private deployment and point the connector to your DB.

[21:00] Priya: Compliance: data residency and retention — can we control retention windows at route level?
[21:08] Lena: Yes, routing and retention policies are configurable. For Hosted we offer region pinning and retention controls; Dedicated and Private give you full control, especially for regulated workloads.

[23:30] Ethan: On pricing — we'd like a cost estimate for expected volumes. Our initial traffic: 5k requests/day, avg 120 tokens per request, spike to 20k/day for promos.
[23:42] Lena: We'll run a cost estimator. For that profile, depending on model and batching, we can give per-month estimate and show Dedicated commit options which reduce unit cost.

[25:00] Samir: Integration work — what does a pilot look like? Time to first integration?
[25:10] Marcus: A quick pilot: 1) Redwood shares SDK + sample repo, 2) you run integration in dev behind gateway, 3) we run small benchmark with representative prompts, 4) iterate on batching/quantization profiles. Typical first integration in 1-2 weeks.

[27:45] Priya: We have security reviewers — can you provide SOC2 report, data flow diagram, and KMS integration docs?
[27:53] Lena: Yes, will share SOC 2 and a security pack. Marcus will include the KMS & VPC setup guide.

[29:20] Ethan: Any limitations with LangChain chains that rely on streaming token-level callback hooks?
[29:28] Marcus: Our SDK exposes streaming callbacks compatible with LangChain "streaming" callbacks; minor naming mismatch sometimes in the examples (Langchain vs LangChain), but functionally supported. We also have an off-the-shelf provider class for LangChain.

[31:40] Priya: If we go Dedicated vs Hosted what's the migration path later?
[31:48] Lena: You can start hosted and migrate to Dedicated with a config change and traffic cutover; models and prompts stay the same since the API surface is consistent. For Private we'd need an on-prem setup and a slightly longer lead time.

[33:00] Samir: About proxies — do you recommend putting Redwood behind our existing rate-limiting proxy (we use Kong)?
[33:07] Marcus: Kong is fine; you can implement the token-exchange plugin and have Kong call Redwood with short-lived tokens. We have community examples for Envoy/Kong.

[35:10] Ethan: Observability again — can we get sample dashboards for cost/latency per route?
[35:17] Marcus: Yes, we have dashboard templates for Grafana and sample Prometheus queries. I'll attach them.

[37:00] Priya: Any concerns about model drift and quality regressions? How do you monitor prompt/eval regressions?
[37:10] Marcus: Redwood Optimize has eval hooks — you can run prompt sets, compare outputs across model versions, and get regression alerts. We can tie alerts to rollbacks or automatic fallback to a previous model.

[39:20] Ethan: If we need to use LlamaIndex offline — are embeddings consistent between hosted and private?
[39:28] Marcus: Yes we ensure inference behavior is consistent; there can be slight differences if you use different quantization or hardware, we'll document those.

[41:00] Priya: Compliance checklist — can you put together a one-pager with answers and responsible contacts?
[41:08] Lena: We'll do that, include security, legal, and an estimated timeline for Private deployment if needed.

[43:30] Ethan: Who will be our point for technical follow-ups?
[43:34] Lena: Marcus will be SE owner. For procurement and pricing it's me.

[44:10] Marcus: Quick recap — we'll share LangChain/LlamaIndex sample code, security pack (SOC2, KMS), Grafana dashboard templates, and a pricing estimate. You'll share traffic profile and security contacts. We'll schedule SE deep dive next week.

[44:45] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[44:50] Lena: Thanks — we'll follow up with materials.
